question: Your extraction system processes 20,000 invoices per week and validates each output against a JSON schema. A verification pass then compares each extracted field with the source document and flags possible errors. The human reviewers can check only a small share of these findings. How should you design the verification pass so that reviewer time goes to the findings most likely to be real errors?

options.text: Have the verification pass report a confidence score with each finding, and route findings to human reviewers using a fixed 0.9 threshold without any calibration.
options.reason: The guide requires calibrating confidence scores against labeled validation sets; an uncalibrated fixed threshold may not match actual error rates.

options.text: Have the verification pass return one pass or fail verdict per document, and send every document that fails to the human reviewers for a full manual check.
options.reason: A single document-level verdict gives no confidence per finding, so findings cannot be routed by calibrated confidence and reviewer time is not focused.

options.text: Have the verification pass report a confidence score with each finding, calibrate thresholds on a labeled validation set, and route low-confidence findings to human reviewers.
options.reason: Self-reported confidence per finding enables calibrated review routing, and the guide calls for calibrating confidence with labeled validation sets.

options.text: Have the same extraction session re-check its own output in a second pass, and route a record to the human reviewers only when the two passes disagree on any extracted field value.
options.reason: A session that keeps its generation reasoning context is less likely to question its own decisions, so self-review misses subtle errors and gives no calibrated routing signal.
